reply.thought: The handoff claims all three refunds were applied, but I need to verify against the refunds table itself before paying anyone. Checking list_refunds first.
The refunds table matches all three requested refunds exactly: orders 180, 181, and 184 with the correct amounts. Next I need the list of orders to find which customers to pay.
The refunds table matches all three requested refunds, so I can proceed. The orders cover three customers (acme, birch, cobalt), and I need each one's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 13345 cents. Acme has orders 180 (16857) and 183 (10279), total 27136, minus refund 180 (13791) gives 13345, which matches. Recording acme's payout now.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next is birch, which is the second customer in the order list, so I'll get its net balance from net_balance rather than computing it myself.
Birch's net balance is 19909 cents. Orders 181 (26275) and 184 (14656) total 40931, minus refunds 181 (17092) and 184 (3930) gives 19909, which matches. Recording birch's payout.
Acme and birch are paid. The last customer in the batch is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance from net_balance before recording its payout.
Cobalt's orders 182 (26600) and 185 (4869) total 31469, and no refunds apply to cobalt, so the net balance of 31469 matches. Recording cobalt's payout.
All three customers have been paid: acme, birch, and cobalt. Each net balance matched my hand check against the orders and refunds, and every record_payout returned ok. The batch is complete.
